summary: A reading of survivalist Kurt Saxon's self-published 1970s magazine The Survivor, which mixed old DIY guides with bomb-making plugs, racist asides and a column warning politicians that gun control would be answered with bombs.

evidence.note: host dates the self-published magazine to 1976
ad for Saxon's improvised weapons and explosives book
op-ed threatening that gun bans will lead dissidents to bomb politicians
hosts discuss Saxon's place in the anti-government racist right
Saxon's review of the film Taxi Driver read at length
reprinted 19th-century medicine recipes sold as a book
reader letter about setting off smoke bombs at school using the book

notes: Media-reading of one issue of The Survivor; the transcript gives 1976 and a Taxi Driver review fixes the date, but issue range is approximate. Primary theme could equally be weapons-arms-trade; no theme for survivalism/prepping. Lifespan of Saxon (born Donald Sisco) from general knowledge, not the transcript. Sirhan and Bremer are only cited inside an op-ed, so 1968-72 not covered.
